title: Step 2 Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · #340 restructure step 2: split hook.py into a core module and six part modules · house-rules 2.69.0 to 2.70.0

short.lead: This is the build plan for step 2 of the restructure, issue #340 (Restructure step 2: move today's hook.py into the core and six part modules, changing nothing). On the design page docs/plans/2026-10-20-restructure-step-2-split.html, question 1 asked how hook.py should split. You chose answer A: real modules now, meaning separate Python files, not just labelled sections. The inventory of every block of hook.py and where it goes is in docs/4-systems/plugin-restructure.md, under "Step 2: how hook.py splits". Nothing is dropped in this step. The work is 4 sub-issues under #340. Each is built by one helper agent, one at a time. Each agent works in its own worktree, which is a separate checked-out copy of the repo on its own branch, so its changes stay apart from the main copy until they are merged.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates or changes and what it needs.
items: file
Step 2a
The house_rules package and the core module (#357)
A package (a folder of Python modules) named scripts/house_rules/, placed beside hook.py. It holds seven modules: core, safe git, session triage, design loop, writing, delegation and docs.

The core module gets the shared helper functions (hook.py:1-141). It also gets nine hook functions, each the function that responds to one kind of hook event: inject, showrule, profile, standards, versioncheck, scope, artifact, runnable and promptran.

hook.py keeps main(), the function that receives each hook event and picks the hook function for it. It imports the moved hook functions, so run.sh and the 32 entries in hooks/hooks.json don't change.
A part module imports only from the core, never from another part.
Nothing from you. Done when verify.py passes twice.
lock
Step 2b
The safe git and docs modules (#358)
Safe git gets guard, guardwrite, branchnudge, prompttimer, the attribution and credit checks, guardgithub and the commit-obligation helpers.
Docs gets docstiers, harvest, the staged-docs check from guard and parity's check.
One test, at verify.py:3236, temporarily replaces a function with a stand-in. It replaces _read_back_body, and after this step it does so on the safe git module instead of on hook.py.
Nothing from you. Depends on step 2a. Done when verify.py passes twice.
hammer
Step 2c
The delegation, design loop and writing modules (#359)
Delegation gets the helper-agent hook functions: delegate, subagentrules, announce, verdict, agentcap, subagentcommit, autosave, commitgate, worktreesweep, audit and userpromptaudit.
Design loop gets the issue workflow, stages and labels, issuelist, the author and issues guards, the end-of-reply checkpoints and pagecheck.
Writing gets the plain-summary, long-reply, visual and editor helpers and the page writing note.

The end-of-reply hook function stays in hook.py as a dispatcher, meaning it only decides which checks to run and calls each part module's check. Separately, the session triage module is created empty, because its content arrives in step 9 (#347).
Nothing from you. Depends on step 2a. Done when verify.py passes twice and hook.py holds only main() and the end-of-reply dispatcher.
check
Step 2d
Changed test lines, version, docs and QA (#360)
Every changed line in verify.py is listed with its reason. Only tests that load or replace a name inside hook.py change.
The plugin goes from 2.69.0 to 2.70.0.
docs/architecture.md and the systems doc name the module that owns each hook function.
A QA page, then a pull request to main once you pass it.
You: read the QA page and answer "QA passed: restructure step 2" or "QA failed: restructure step 2".

changes: The 32 hook entries, run.sh and every check stay.
211 of verify.py's tests run hook.py through run.sh, and none of them change. 6 other tests load hook.py directly. Those 6 change only in where they look up a name.
8,588 lines become a short dispatcher plus seven modules.
One file answers every hook event
hook.py dispatches; each part's module holds its own hook functions
The inventory in docs/4-systems/plugin-restructure.md lists every block's line range and its new module.
A core and six part modules in scripts/house_rules/
Each part can be left out on its own by step 10 (#348)
